newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch central bank says bought guilders Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Dutch central bank says bought guilders Wednesday.

text.p: The Dutch central bank said on Thursday it had bought guilders from other European central banks on Wednesday.
Spokesman Bert Groothof said the transactions, which coincided with a reversal of the Dutch currency's fall against the German mark, were instigated by the other central banks.
"Other central banks sold guilders to us," he told Reuters, adding this was part of a "market operation".
A money market dealer told Reuters the Dutch central bank had bought 800 million guilders in a transaction with another European central bank.
Market sources said the bank bought guilders against marks.
The guilder touched a near four-year low on Tuesday as the mark rose to 1.1269 guilders, breaking through its parity rate under the European exchange rate mechansim of 1.1267.
This move sparked speculation that the central bank may be forced to raise the the special advances rate, which sets the tone for money market rates, in a bid to prop up the currency.
But the guilder strengthened on Wednesday to 1.1263, a level it held in late trading on Thursday.
The Dutch central bank left the special advances rate unchanged at 3.00 percent on Thursday.
Groothof denied the central bank's purchase of guilders was intended as an intervention to prop up the currency.
"It's just a lucky coincidence," he said.
Explaining the desire of other central banks to sell the Dutch currency, he said at least one other European country had issued bonds denominated in guilders in the past.
